Notes: Brussels joint lists existed: CVP-PSC (12), PVV-PLP (4), PLP(Bxl) (3), PSB(Bxl) (7); RW and FDF also ran a joint list (FDF-RW 12). PC+KP are language lists of the Communist Party.
FDF seats (14) were on joint 'FDF–PDLP' lists; UDP=Democratic and Progressive Union (2).

Socialists split: BSP (Flanders) 27, PSB (Wallonia) 34. Liberals split: PVV (Flanders) 17, PRLW (Wallonia) 16. FDF 11. PCB 2. RW 4. One PSB–RW joint list (1) existed but is not separately assigned here.
First election after PS/SP split. VB participates for the first time (1 seat). UDRT wins 1 seat.
Voting age lowered to 18. Greens enter: Ecolo 2, Agalev 2. FDF–RW joint list 8 seats. VB listed with 1 seat.
Incumbent Martens V coalition (CVP/PSC + PVV/PRL) continued. Greens grew; VB held 1 seat.
Snap election after Voeren crisis. Liberals ran as PVV (Flanders) and PRL (Wallonia). Greens: Agalev 6, Ecolo 3. VB 2; FDF 3.
‘Black Sunday’—far-right surge. Separate PVV-PLP joint list. Source: Wikipedia Chamber table.
First election with 150-seat Chamber after 1993 state reform. PRL–FDF is a joint list.
‘Dioxin affair’; first liberal-led coalition since 1930s. PRL–FDF joint list.
5% threshold introduced; Greens hit hard (Agalev 0). MR launched 2002. N-VA first seat.
CD&V–N-VA alliance largest list; LDD enters; Groen! returns.
N-VA largest party; long government formation (541 days).
N-VA leads; Michel I coalition (N-VA, MR, CD&V, Open Vld). PTB/PVDA gains first 2 seats.
VB resurgence; PTB/PVDA gains 12 seats. ‘Vivaldi’ coalition forms (2020).
Les Engagés replaces cdH; Vooruit replaces sp.a. VB second-largest; N-VA remains largest.
